name: fu
description: Park ideas mid-session, file them under the job you're on, and resume Claude Code or Copilot sessions later
description_good_justification: The README opens with what fu does: park ideas mid-session, file them under the job they belong to, and resume Claude Code or Copilot sessions later. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#readme
interact_justification: The README explains how to install and use it; issues and pull requests are on GitHub, and CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to contribute. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md sets the requirements: test first, Conventional Commits, checks passing, a code-owner review. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/LICENSE>.
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
documentation_basics_justification: docs/README.md covers how to install, use and securely use fu, linking to the README sections: https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: The README documents the commands; `fu --help` and `fu <command> --help` describe every command and flag; the agent skill is documented in src/fu/skills/follow-ups/SKILL.md. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#use
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
repo_interim_justification: All work is committed on branches and merged through pull requests; interim versions between releases are in the public git history. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version, e.g. v0.1.0. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/releases
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged in git (v0.1.0). https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/tags
release_notes_justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md>.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in any release yet.
report_process_justification: Non-trivial SECURITY[.md] file found file in repository: <https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md>. [osps_do_02_01]
report_responses_justification: No bug reports have been filed yet (new project); the maintainer watches GitHub Issues and will respond.
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement requests have been filed yet (new project); the maintainer watches GitHub Issues and will respond.
report_archive_justification: Reports and responses are in GitHub Issues, which are public and searchable. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md explains how to report a vulnerability privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting: https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reporting through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, described in SECURITY.md. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received yet. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledge within 7 days.
build_floss_tools_justification: Built with FLOSS tools only: Python, uv and hatchling (`uv build`).
test_justification: A pytest suite (263 tests) runs with `make test`, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the README. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/tree/main/tests
test_invocation_justification: `make test` (or `uv run pytest`), the standard way to run Python tests.
test_most_justification: The suite covers 90% of the code (pytest-cov), including the CLI, the board logic and the TUI driven headlessly.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: "Test first. Add a failing test, then the code. Every bug fix gets a regression test." https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: Major changes have added tests alongside the code, as the commit history shows. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/commits/main
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is in CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: ruff lints with the pycodestyle, pyflakes, bugbear, pyupgrade, bandit (S) and simplify rule sets; CodeQL also runs. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/pyproject.toml
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any ruff warning or formatting difference, so warnings are fixed before merging.
warnings_strict_justification: ruff with bugbear, bandit and pyupgrade rules; CI fails on any warning.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles here: a small attack surface (local data only, no network service), least privilege (read-only CI tokens, pinned actions), shell-quoted restart commands, and a documented trust boundary for board.json (README, SECURITY.md).
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common errors for this kind of software, such as shell injection, unsafe deserialization and leaked secrets, and guards against them: commands are built with shell quoting, YAML is loaded with safe_load, ruff bandit rules and CodeQL run in CI, and gitleaks scans history.
crypto_published_justification: fu does not use cryptography. (Releases are signed in CI with Sigstore, which is not part of the software.)
crypto_random_justification: fu does not use cryptography or generate keys or nonces.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are downloaded over HTTPS from GitHub; the Homebrew formula pins a SHA-256 checksum, and releases carry Sigstore attestations and SLSA provenance.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities. OSV-Scanner and Dependabot check dependencies in CI.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: There are no known vulnerabilities. Dependabot alerts, OSV-Scanner and CodeQL report new ones.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL and ruff bandit (S) rules run on every pull request.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no open exploitable medium or higher findings. The one medium CodeQL alert, the SLSA generator referenced by tag, is a documented, deliberate exception (docs/adr/0006).
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL and ruff run on every push and pull request, and CodeQL also runs weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or other dynamic analysis tool is used beyond the test suite.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: fu is written in Python, a memory-safe language.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No separate dynamic analysis configuration is used.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run, so there are no findings to fix.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the tests, lint and security checks on every push and pull request, on Linux and macOS. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/actions/workflows/ci.yml
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans the full history in CI and on pre-push; GitHub secret scanning and push protection are on.
english_justification: All documentation is in English and English bug reports are accepted.
hardening_justification: Atomic writes, safe YAML loading, quoting of every shell field, no network code, and argument lists instead of a shell for other programs.
installation_common_justification: brew install josh-quinn/tap/fu and brew uninstall fu; or pip/uv tool install of the wheel.
dco_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off: a prepare-commit-msg hook adds it, CI rejects pull request commits without it, and web commits require sign-off. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md [osps_le_01_01]
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the governance model: a single maintainer who decides, ADRs for hard-to-reverse decisions, and how access is granted. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
code_of_conduct_justification: Contributor Covenant in the standard location. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md "Roles" names who holds each role and its access and responsibilities. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
bus_factor_justification: fu has one maintainer, so the bus factor is 1. GOVERNANCE.md sets out how a second maintainer would be added. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md: what is planned and not planned until November 2027. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: docs/architecture.md, with the decisions in docs/adr. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/architecture.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md "What you can expect" lists the security requirements fu meets and what it does not protect against. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md#what-you-can-expect
documentation_current_justification: Documentation changes land in the same pull request as the code they describe (CONTRIBUTING.md); the README, SECURITY.md and docs were updated for the current release.
documentation_achievements_justification: The README front page shows and links the OpenSSF Best Practices, Baseline and Scorecard badges. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#readme
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: fu is a keyboard-only CLI and TUI with plain-text output that works with terminal screen readers, and every TUI key is listed in the README and the in-app help. Project sites are GitHub pages.
internationalization_justification: The interface is English-only by design (ROADMAP.md "Not planned"); fu is a personal productivity tool without a localisation audience yet.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub and bestpractices.dev; the project stores no passwords.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Upgrade with brew upgrade fu; old boards load, and an old config.toml is converted once with a message. The README documents upgrade and uninstall. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#install
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerabilities have been resolved in the last 12 months. SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters unless they ask for anonymity.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md "How we respond": acknowledge, assess, fix, release, publish. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md "Code style": PEP 8 via ruff format and the ruff rules in pyproject.toml; POSIX sh checked by shellcheck. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff check and ruff format --check run in make check and fail CI on any difference.
build_standard_variables_justification: fu is pure Python and builds no native binaries.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Pure Python; there are no debug symbols to strip.
build_non_recursive_justification: uv build with hatchling builds a single Python package; there is no recursive build.
build_repeatable_justification: Builds are bit-for-bit reproducible: building tag v0.1.0 locally gives the same SHA-256 as the released sdist and wheel, and CI rebuilds and compares on every change. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#verify-a-release
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installed through Homebrew or Python packaging tools, which honour their standard prefix and destination settings (e.g. HOMEBREW_PREFIX, pip --prefix/--root).
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, then uv sync and make check set up the code, dependencies and tests (CONTRIBUTING.md "Building from source"). https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
external_dependencies_justification: pyproject.toml and uv.lock list the dependencies in a machine-readable form; releases also carry an SPDX SBOM. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/pyproject.toml
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot alerts and updates, OSV-Scanner in CI, and dependency review on every pull request.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: All third-party code comes from PyPI through uv.lock, so updating is uv lock --upgrade-package; nothing is vendored.
interfaces_current_justification: ruff pyupgrade (UP) rules flag deprecated Python APIs, and CI runs on current Python versions (3.11 to 3.14).
automated_integration_testing_justificat: GitHub Actions runs the full test suite on every push and pull request and reports pass or fail. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/actions/workflows/ci.yml
regression_tests_added50_justification: Every bug fix comes with a regression test (CONTRIBUTING.md), e.g. the session-id and failed-save fixes in PR #5.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement coverage is 93% (pytest-cov), measured on every make check run.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md "Ground rules": test first, and every bug fix gets a regression test. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
implement_secure_design_justification: The assurance case shows how each secure design principle is applied. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/security/threat-model.md
input_validation_justification: CLI choices are allowlisted by argparse, session ids by a strict pattern, and config values (e.g. the key modifier) against fixed sets; invalid input is rejected. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/security/threat-model.md
crypto_credential_agility_justification: fu stores no credentials or keys.
signed_releases_justification: Releases are signed with Sigstore build-provenance attestations and SLSA provenance, keyless, from GitHub Actions; the README documents verifying them and the expected signer identity. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#verify-a-release
version_tags_signed_justification: Tags are not yet signed; the maintainer has no signing key configured. Releases themselves are signed (see signed_releases).
assurance_case_justification: docs/security/threat-model.md: threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles and the common weaknesses countered, each tied to a test or check. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/security/threat-model.md
OSPS-AC-02.01_justification: A personal GitHub repository: collaborators are added only by the owner inviting them by hand, and there are none. GOVERNANCE.md says the repo moves to an organisation, so roles can start at Read/Triage, before anyone else gets access. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
OSPS-AC-03.01_justification: An active repository ruleset on main requires a pull request and the required status checks; a direct push is rejected (verified, GH013).
OSPS-AC-03.02_justification: The repository ruleset on main restricts deletion and blocks force pushes.
OSPS-BR-01.01_justification: Workflows never interpolate github.event values into run: scripts; untrusted values go through env: (zizmor template-injection audit runs in CI with no findings). https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/.github/workflows/security.yml
OSPS-BR-07.01_justification: gitleaks scans the full history in CI and on pre-push; GitHub secret scanning and push protection are on. [no_leaked_credentials]

OSPS-DO-02.01_justification: Non-trivial SECURITY[.md] file found file in repository: <https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md>.
OSPS-GV-02.01_justification: GitHub supports public discussions on proposed changes (via pull requests) and usage obstacles (via issues).
OSPS-LE-02.01_justification: The MIT license for the repository contents is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
OSPS-LE-02.02_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI). [floss_license]
OSPS-LE-03.02_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/LICENSE>. [license_location]

OSPS-QA-01.02_justification: Repository git metadata is publicly available on GitHub.

OSPS-QA-04.01_justification: The README lists the project repositories: josh-quinn/fu (source) and josh-quinn/homebrew-tap (formula). https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#repositories

OSPS-QA-05.02_justification: No unreviewable binary artifacts are in version control; the repository is source, docs and config text only.
OSPS-VM-02.01_justification: SECURITY.md explains how to report a vulnerability privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting: https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md [vulnerability_report_process]
OSPS-AC-04.01_justification: The repository default GITHUB_TOKEN permission is read-only, every workflow sets top-level permissions: contents: read, and jobs widen only what they need. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/tree/main/.github/workflows
OSPS-BR-02.01_justification: Each release has a unique version, e.g. v0.1.0. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/releases [version_unique]
OSPS-BR-04.01_justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md>. [release_notes]
OSPS-BR-05.01_justification: Dependencies are installed with uv from the committed uv.lock (uv sync --locked); GitHub Actions are pinned by commit SHA; no curl-pipe-to-shell installs.
OSPS-BR-06.01_justification: Each release has a Sigstore build-provenance attestation (actions/attest-build-provenance), SLSA provenance and SHA256SUMS. Verify with gh attestation verify ... --signer-workflow josh-quinn/fu/.github/workflows/release.yml. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#verify-a-release

OSPS-GV-01.01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md lists everyone with access to sensitive resources (the sole maintainer). https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
OSPS-GV-01.02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md describes the roles and responsibilities of maintainer and contributors. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
OSPS-GV-03.02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md sets the requirements: test first, Conventional Commits, checks passing, a code-owner review. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md [contribution_requirements]

OSPS-SA-01.01_justification: docs/architecture.md describes the components and their interactions; ADRs in docs/adr record the design decisions. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/architecture.md
OSPS-SA-02.01_justification: The README documents the commands; `fu --help` and `fu <command> --help` describe every command and flag; the agent skill is documented in src/fu/skills/follow-ups/SKILL.md. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#use [documentation_interface]
OSPS-SA-03.01_justification: docs/security/threat-model.md is the security assessment: assets, trust boundaries, threats and mitigations, reviewed each minor release. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/security/threat-model.md
OSPS-VM-03.01_justification: Private reporting through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, described in SECURITY.md. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/security/advisories/new [vulnerability_report_private]
OSPS-VM-04.01_justification: SECURITY.md: confirmed vulnerabilities are published as GitHub Security Advisories with a CVE, and noted in the CHANGELOG. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-AC-04.02_justification: Every job in every workflow declares its own permissions, granting only what that job needs (e.g. contents: write and id-token: write only in the release job). https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/tree/main/.github/workflows
OSPS-BR-02.02_justification: Each release has a unique version, e.g. v0.1.0. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/releases [version_unique]
OSPS-BR-07.02_justification: docs/security/secrets-policy.md defines how secrets are stored, accessed and rotated; CI uses only short-lived GITHUB_TOKEN and OIDC credentials. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/security/secrets-policy.md
OSPS-DO-03.01_justification: The README "Verify a release" section gives the commands to check each release archive with gh attestation verify and slsa-verifier. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#verify-a-release
OSPS-DO-03.02_justification: The verification commands pin the expected signer: --signer-workflow josh-quinn/fu/.github/workflows/release.yml and --source-uri/--source-tag for slsa-verifier. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu#verify-a-release
OSPS-DO-04.01_justification: SECURITY.md "Supported versions": only the latest release is supported. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-DO-05.01_justification: SECURITY.md: a release reaches end of life, with no further fixes, when the next one is published. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-GV-04.01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md "Giving someone more access" sets the vetting process before anyone gets escalated permissions. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
OSPS-QA-02.02_justification: Each release attaches an SPDX SBOM generated from the locked dependencies (anchore/sbom-action). https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/releases
OSPS-QA-04.02_justification: fu has no subprojects; the only other repository, josh-quinn/homebrew-tap, is a distribution channel holding a generated formula.
OSPS-QA-06.02_justification: A pytest suite (263 tests) runs with `make test`, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the README. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/tree/main/tests [test]
OSPS-QA-06.03_justification: The test-first policy is in CONTRIBUTING.md, and the pull request template asks for tests. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md [tests_documented_added]
OSPS-QA-07.01_justification: fu has a single maintainer, so changes are merged by their author after all required checks pass. Non-author approval will be required once there is a second maintainer (GOVERNANCE.md).
OSPS-SA-03.02_justification: docs/security/threat-model.md is a STRIDE threat model of assets, trust boundaries, threats and mitigations. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/docs/security/threat-model.md
OSPS-VM-04.02_justification: SECURITY.md commits to publishing OpenVEX statements in docs/security/vex/ for dependency vulnerabilities that do not affect fu; none have been needed so far. https://github.com/josh-quinn/fu/blob/main/SECURITY.md
OSPS-VM-05.03_justification: Per SECURITY-INSIGHTS.yml: repository.security.tools type=SCA with integration.ci=true
